surface_verification.justification: P3.1 is dormant infrastructure (SPEC §8 E1 / §5 'no downstream effect') -- a pure Python library (lib.ac_identity) and CLI tool (mint_ac_ids.py) with no startable web/dev-server surface of its own and not wired into any consumer yet; the golden-corpus unit tests (shared/tests/test_ac_identity*.py) and the CLI subprocess tests (shared/scripts/tools/tests/test_mint_ac_ids.py) ARE the verification, matching how prior tooling-only iterates in this repo's history were verified.

behaviors.behavior: AC1: AC ids are minted by a tool (mint()), in document order, zero-padded, never hand-typed
AC1: the minting CLI (mint_ac_ids.py) dry-runs by default and only writes under --write
AC2: read()/read_all() parse the shipped FR heading+bullet shape and pair each criterion with its minted id
AC2: read() composes on lib.fr_criteria (R0) for continuation-line joining rather than reimplementing it

AC2: golden corpus pins boundary shapes (blank lines between bullets, same-rank heading terminates the block, a deeper heading disqualifies the leading-bullet run, a second FR heading starts a new block) for BOTH mint() and read(), round-tripped
behaviors.evidence: `test_a_blank_line_between_two_bullets_does_not_break_bullet_detection`, `test_a_same_rank_non_fr_heading_ends_the_fr_block`, `test_a_deeper_heading_ends_the_leading_bullet_run_though_not_the_block`, `test_a_second_fr_heading_starts_a_new_block_immediately` PASSED -- the deeper-heading case is a genuine mint/read divergence the round-trip design was built to catch (external code review, GLM medium), fixed by making mint()'s bullet-discovery gate mirror read()'s adjacency gate exactly

behaviors.behavior: AC2: read()/read_all() agree with mint() on scope -- neither scans the legacy bold-anchor form fr_criteria still tolerates
behaviors.evidence: `test_a_legacy_bold_anchor_block_is_out_of_scope_for_read_too` PASSED -- openai external-review medium finding, fixed

behaviors.behavior: AC3: re-running the minter on its own output is a no-op (idempotent)
AC3: inserting a bullet in the middle of an already-minted list never renumbers the existing ids
AC3: deleting a minted bullet never frees its number for reuse; a stale-vs-ahead registry snapshot self-heals via bidirectional max-seeding

A marker that cannot be trusted (non-canonical digits, [AC00], near-miss shapes like [AC 1]/[ac01], stacked markers, duplicate id under one FR) is rejected loudly by both mint() and read(), never silently coerced
A negative/non-int registry value is rejected by both the CLI loader and mint() itself, never used to mint [AC00]
behaviors.evidence: `test_a_negative_registry_value_is_rejected_not_used_to_mint_ac00` (lib), `test_a_negative_registry_value_exits_non_zero_not_a_hand_typed_ac00`, `test_a_non_integer_registry_value_exits_non_zero_not_a_bare_traceback_deep_in_mint` (CLI) PASSED -- external code review findings, fixed

behaviors.behavior: A duplicate-marker document makes the CLI exit non-zero, not silently exit 0
Concurrent --write invocations on the same registry file are serialized by a file lock, never race the same next AC id
behaviors.evidence: code path exercised by every CLI subprocess test (each acquires and releases the lock in mint_ac_ids.py); openai external-review high finding, fixed via lib.file_lock.file_lock()

behaviors.behavior: --write persists the registry before the spec, so an interrupted write can only leave a harmless gap, never a reuse
behaviors.evidence: `test_write_creates_the_registry_file_even_when_the_spec_has_no_bullets` PASSED (registry-write path exercised); ordering itself is a write-order property recorded in the ADR's External-Code-Review-Findings table, not independently re-orderable in a unit test without fault injection
